target.note: ALEV III spectral sensitivity ESTIMATE (not a measurement), data/alexa/target.json

provenance.fit_solver: scipy 1.18.1 optimize.least_squares(method='lm', analytic Jacobian, xtol=1e-15, ftol=1e-15, gtol=1e-15, max_nfev=500) from the Y^(-2/3) weighted-RGB solution, then up to 8 Gauss-Newton steps (stop below 1e-13); numpy 2.5.3
provenance.duv_scale_method: at every 100 K: median over green excess/deficit tilts of +-5 % and +-10 % (training/sensor_map/lights.py tint_spd) of the locus light, of |CIE 1960 uv offset| / |log-chroma offset|, both perpendicular to the locus (tangent from lights 3 % either side); log-chroma of the camera curves in the published raw scale (see light_conventions)
provenance.light_conventions: blackbody below 4000 K and CIE D series from 4000 K (rawtoaces); mired = 1e6/CCT with CCT the generating temperature for blackbody and D series and the Ohno (2013) CCT of the SPD for F and LED lights; SPDs 380-780 nm at 5 nm, peak-normalised; camera RGB scale: locus (log-chroma) and duv_scale tables are computed from the camera's spectral curves in the published raw scale (clipped at 0, NOT normalised per channel; one common factor per camera, green peak 1.0, red and blue peaks as published) so a locus point is the raw white of the light and compares directly with as-shot gains, Pick white and the illuminant estimator; sensor_map matrices are computed from the same curves peak-normalised per channel (scale-free: every response is divided by the response to the white of the same curves); alexa_white tables are from the ALEXA estimate, peak-normalised by construction (only ratios enter the chain)
provenance.cie_data: CIE SPDs (D series, F1-F12, LED-B1..B5, LED-BH1, LED-RGB1, LED-V1, LED-V2; CC BY-SA 4.0, via colour-science) and the CIE 1931 observer were used at fit time only; this file holds fitted coefficients and tables derived from them, not the SPDs. Pending HUMAN M1-H4 (docs/14): confirm that CIE-derived coefficient tables may ship.
